```python
def _downstream_closure(failing: set[str], groups: list[WorkGroup]) -> set[str]:
    """Forward-reachable task set from `failing`: each failing task plus every
    task in any downstream (dependent) WorkGroup. Bounds re-execution so a bad
    upstream task re-runs its dependents, but untouched work is preserved."""
    task_group: dict[str, str] = {}
    by_id = {g.id: g for g in groups}
    dependents: dict[str, list[str]] = {g.id: [] for g in groups}
    for g in groups:
        for t in g.tasks:
            task_group[t.id] = g.id
        for d in g.depends_on:
            if d in dependents:
                dependents[d].append(g.id)
    out: set[str] = set(failing)
    stack = [task_group[t] for t in failing if t in task_group]
    seen: set[str] = set()
    while stack:
        gid = stack.pop()
        if gid in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(gid)
        for dep in dependents[gid]:
            for t in by_id[dep].tasks:
                out.add(t.id)
            stack.append(dep)
    return out
```

85: def _seed_stack(failing: set[str], task_group: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
86:     """Return group IDs for all failing tasks that have a known group."""

90: def _traverse_dependents(stack: list[str], by_id: dict[str, WorkGroup], dependents: dict[str, list[str]]) -> set[str]:
91:     """Walk the dependency graph from the stack, collecting all reachable task IDs."""
92:     out: set[str] = set(stack)
93:     seen: set[str] = set()
94:     while stack:
95:         gid = stack.pop()
96:         if gid in seen:
97:             continue
98:         seen.add(gid)
99:         for dep in dependents[gid]:
100:             for t in by_id[dep].tasks:
101:                 out.add(t.id)
102:             stack.append(dep)
103:     return out

106: def red_team_passed(findings: list[dict], rubric_cells: list[dict]) -> bool:
107:     """Deterministic red-team go/no-go verdict — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH.
108: 
109:     Used by BOTH `run_red_team_gate` and the inline `passed()` reviewer check
110:     so the gating logic can never drift between the two code paths (and never
111:     contradict red_team.yaml).
112: 
113:     Gate is driven SOLELY by:
114:       * `findings` (task-keyed, severity == "blocker") -> which tasks to recode,
115:       * an unresolvable global blocker in `rubric_cube` (a blocker cell with no
116:         matching `findings` entry) -> HARD FAIL.
117:     The LLM's free `green` boolean is NEVER trusted. This is exactly the
118:     contract documented in templates/red_team.yaml + customised/red_team.yaml.
119:     """
120:     failing = any(f.get("severity") == "blocker" for f in findings)
